DigitalOcean’s latest fiscal report reveals a company firing on all cylinders, with AI-native customers and larger enterprise deals propelling both revenue and profitability to new heights.
Not only did the agentic inference cloud provider hit a landmark $1 billion annualized monthly revenue run-rate in December 2025, but management also set the stage for sustained momentum through 2027 with upgraded growth forecasts.

Critical to this growth was a striking 150% year-over-year surge in AI customer annual recurring revenue (ARR), reaching $120 million, while million-dollar customer ARR soared by 123% to $133 million.

DigitalOcean Holdings (NYSE:DOCN) presented its second quarter 2026 earnings results on August 4, 2026, showcasing a dramatic acceleration in growth driven by its AI-native cloud platform.
The company reported revenue growth of 29% year-over-year, more than double the 14% growth rate from the same quarter a year earlier, as AI-focused customers increasingly adopted its integrated infrastructure and inference services.
Despite beating Wall Street expectations with adjusted earnings of $0.45 per share on revenue of $281.2 million, shares initially fell 7.85% in premarket trading before recovering.
The stock has since rebounded to $131.50, up 3.4% from the previous close of $127.17, reflecting investor reassessment of the company’s long-term growth trajectory after a 371% gain over the past year.

{"figures":[{"fact_key":"Start date","value":"2025-09-10"},{"fact_key":"End date","value":"2026-09-09"},{"fact_key":"Total return on contributions","value":188.87},{"fact_key":"Benchmark return","value":12.07},{"fact_key":"Return difference versus benchmark","value":176.8},{"fact_key":"Worst drop from a prior high","value":-42.12},{"fact_key":"Starting capital","value":1000.0},{"fact_key":"Each recurring contribution","value":100.0},{"fact_key":"Total money contributed","value":2300.0},{"fact_key":"Ending portfolio value","value":6644.07},{"fact_key":"Highest portfolio value","value":8648.6},{"fact_key":"Executed fills","value":13},{"fact_key":"Fee per trade","value":10.0},{"fact_key":"Slippage per trade","value":5.0}],"language":"en","text":"From September 10, 2025 through September 9, 2026, this test was a story of a small cloud company becoming closely associated with the artificial intelligence boom. DigitalOcean reported that third-quarter 2025 revenue rose 16 percent to $230 million, annual recurring revenue reached $919 million, and demand was strong enough that it was adding data-center and graphics-chip capacity. Management also said it expected its growth targets to arrive earlier than previously planned. [DigitalOcean's third-quarter results](https://investors.digitalocean.com/news/news-details/2025/DigitalOcean-Announces-Third-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx) support the business-growth part of that explanation.

The optimism continued into the next report. For the fourth quarter, DigitalOcean reported revenue of $242 million, up 18 percent from a year earlier, and said its 2025 revenue reached $901 million. It also raised its outlook for 2026 and highlighted growing demand from AI customers. [The company's full-year results](https://investors.digitalocean.com/news/news-details/2026/DigitalOcean-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Year-2025-Financial-Results/) are evidence that the business was improving. It is reasonable to infer that investors rewarded the shares for the combination of faster growth, larger customers, and AI demand, although those reports cannot explain every daily price move.

By August 2026, the acceleration was more visible. DigitalOcean reported second-quarter revenue of $281.2 million, up about 29 percent year over year, and earnings above the analyst estimate. The shares initially fell after the report before recovering, which shows what holding DOCN was like: good company news could still produce sharp swings because investors were judging the results against very high expectations. [Reporting on the second-quarter results](https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/digitalocean-q2-2026-slides-ai-growth-drives-29-revenue-surge-93CH-4834748) documents that immediate reversal.

The test began with $1,000 and added $100 each month. Across 13 fills, it put $2,300 into DOCN and ended at $6,644.07. That equals a 188.87 percent return on the contributions. The path was not smooth: the portfolio's worst fall from an earlier high was -42.12 percent, and its highest recorded value was $8,648.60. In practical terms, someone holding through the period had to watch a large portion of the gains disappear at one point, without knowing whether the decline would stop. The regular purchases helped spread the entry prices across the year, but they did not remove the risk of a large fall in a single volatile stock. The test also includes small trading costs of 10 basis points in fees and 5 basis points in slippage per trade.

SPY, the benchmark representing a broad basket of large US companies, returned 12.07 percent over the same window. DOCN therefore beat it by 176.8 percentage points. The comparison says more about concentration than about a typical stock experience: one company tied to a powerful AI and cloud theme rose far more than the broad market, but it also exposed the holder to a much deeper setback. The result was excellent for this particular historical period, while the large drawdown shows the price paid for that concentration."}
